get_car_data.description: Get one car's telemetry - speed, throttle, brake, gear, RPM and DRS - sampled about 3.7 times a second. The DRS code and the 0/100 brake reading are decoded into readable fields beside the raw values; DRS left the sport with the 2026 rules, so its fields are empty from then on. A session and a driver are both required because a single car's session is already tens of thousands of samples; narrow it further with a time window or a speed floor.
get_car_data.name: get_car_data

parameters.description: Optional. The race weekend to read. Setting this also fills the Session dropdown with that weekend's sessions. Accepts a key from an earlier step, or 'latest' for the most recent one. A session counts as live until 30 minutes after it ends, and live data needs a paid OpenF1 account, so 'latest' answers from then on.
parameters.name: meeting_key

parameters.description: Required. The session to read telemetry from. Pick a meeting first and this lists its sessions. Accepts a key from an earlier step, or 'latest' for the most recent one. A session counts as live until 30 minutes after it ends, and live data needs a paid OpenF1 account, so 'latest' answers from then on.
parameters.name: session_key

parameters.description: Required. The driver's car number. Telemetry is per-car, and one car's session is already tens of thousands of samples, so a driver must be chosen. Pick a session first and this lists that session's entries.
parameters.name: driver_number

parameters.description: Optional. Only samples at or above this speed - 300 finds the fastest parts of a lap.
parameters.name: min_speed

parameters.description: Optional. Only samples at or below this speed. It cannot be below Minimum speed.
parameters.name: max_speed

parameters.description: Optional. Only samples in this gear, 1 to 8. 0 is neutral or no gear engaged.
parameters.name: n_gear

parameters.description: Optional. Only include records at or after this UTC moment. Narrowing the window is the main way to keep a busy session's result readable.
parameters.name: date_from

parameters.description: Optional. Only include records at or before this UTC moment. It cannot be earlier than From.
parameters.name: date_to

parameters.description: Optional. How many rows to return, 1 to 5000 (default 100). OpenF1 has no paging, so the whole matching set is fetched and cut to this; the result says how many matched in total and whether it was cut.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: How much of each row to print into the run output for a person to read. Every row that was returned is listed either way, however many that is: the Maximum rows field above decides that, not this one. 'One line each' gives the fields that matter for this collection; 'Every field' adds everything else the API sent. This only changes what is displayed, never what is saved - a later step sees the same data whichever is chosen. Defaults to one line each.
parameters.name: output_detail

output_detail.description: How much of each row the run output printed: summary or full.

description:
Read Formula 1 timing and telemetry from OpenF1: the race calendar and session list, entry lists with team colours, classifications and starting grids, championship standings, and how a session actually unfolded - lap and sector times, pit stops, tyre stints, running order, gaps to the car ahead, overtakes, race control's flags and safety cars, trackside weather, and team radio with audio links. Down to the car itself: speed, throttle, brake, gear, RPM, DRS and track position, sampled about 3.7 times a second. Every session from 2023 onward is free and needs no API key.

This is an independent integration. OpenF1 is an unofficial, open-source project and is not associated with the Formula 1 companies; F1, FORMULA 1, GRAND PRIX and related marks are trade marks of Formula One Licensing B.V.
